findings.issue: Round-1 major finding (decision rationale duplicated from the Decisions section into task descriptions) is only one-third addressed. Task 6 (was Task 2) was genuinely fixed — the transient-field paragraph is now the single clause "The existing transient field cannot carry it." But the other two are byte-for-byte unchanged apart from one deleted backtick: Task 2 still says "leaving degraded sentinels and identifier fields plain so a missing signal stays visually distinct from a real number", which restates the Rationale of Decision 9 ("Bold must read as 'there is a real number here', which is why degraded fields stay plain"); Task 7 still says "reserving space for the field so an overlong prompt is truncated rather than covered", which restates the Decision of Decision 3 ("Truncate the prompt, never overlay it with the input field"). The renumbering makes this worse rather than better: the rationale now lives in two places under two different numbers, and Decision 9's number already drifted once in this round.
findings.fix: Trim to WHAT + a pointer: Task 2 -> "...leaving `n/a` sentinels and identifier fields plain (Decision 9)."; Task 7 -> "...deriving both axes from the real state (Decisions 3 and 11)." The dropped clauses already exist verbatim in the Decisions section, so nothing is lost.

findings.issue: Task 8 (Wave 4, stand verification) now carries a code-fixing mandate — "Fix any defect found, or ... report it and stop for a decision" — while keeping `Skill: pre-deploy-qa` and `Reviewers: none`. The catalog scopes `pre-deploy-qa` to "Acceptance testing before deploy (tests + acceptance criteria)" and assigns it no reviewers precisely because "QA is its own verification" — i.e. the empty reviewer set is sound only for a task that does not write code. As written, a fix landing in `top/stat.go` or `top/dialog.go` during Wave 4 would ship without `dev-code-reviewer` or `dev-test-reviewer` ever seeing it, and Task 9 (also `pre-deploy-qa`) is not a code review. This is new in round 2 — round 1's Task 8 only ran the stand. The round-1 fix asked for the stand run to be sequenced ahead of the Final Wave, which was done correctly; the added fix-it-yourself mandate is what creates the gap.
findings.fix: Pick one. (a) Scope Task 8 to observation: "...record every defect found and stop", `Files to modify: none`, and let a follow-up code-writing task (or a repeat of the owning wave task) carry the fix under normal review. (b) Keep the fix mandate but declare it honestly: `Skill: code-writing`, `Reviewers: dev-code-reviewer, dev-test-reviewer`, and state in the description that the task begins with a stand run. Option (a) matches the catalog better and keeps Wave 4 a pure gate.

findings.issue: Task 1's scope is narrower than what its own verification demands. The description covers only the blank line, but the per-task verification row for Task 1 requires "guard threshold 12", Testing Strategy requires "`topBandLayout`: the three changed cases plus the new height-guard threshold of 12", and Backward Compatibility lists the 13->12 drop as one of only two user-visible default changes in the feature. Removing a row and lowering the guard are related but not the same edit, and a decomposed task file built from the description alone would omit the second.
findings.fix: Add a clause to Task 1's description: "...and lower the verbose height guard from 13 to 12 rows, since one fewer row is now consumed." Keeps the task at two sentences.

summary: Approved — all three round-1 criticals are genuinely resolved, and no new critical was introduced. Wave partitioning is now correct and verifiable: I recomputed the file sets per wave and no file appears twice in any wave (W1: layout/stat/config_view+keybindings+help; W2: config+config_view+stat vs ui+top+dialog; W3: config+top+ui+config_view+stat vs dialog), the wave-partition table matches the task bodies exactly, the Risks row was rewritten to state the parallel-execution-in-one-working-tree reasoning instead of asserting the old overlaps were harmless, and cross-wave file reuse (stat.go in 1/2/3, dialog.go in 2/3, config_view.go in 1/2/3) is sequential and therefore fine. Dependency direction matches wave order everywhere: task 7 needs task 5 (W2) and task 1 (W1); task 6 needs task 5; task 9 needs task 8, now one wave earlier; no cycles. The stand run owns Wave 4 alone with the single-tmux-session reasoning stated, and Task 9 has both a Verify line and a per-task verification row, closing the last round-1 verification gap. Renumbering is internally consistent (Decisions 1..14 in document order, tasks 1..9, verification rows 1..9 all matching their tasks). Template compliance re-checked from scratch and holds: frontmatter valid (2026-08-02 / draft / feature/tui-papercuts / M), every required section present and substantive, Risks a real table, no time-based estimates anywhere, 9 tasks well under the split threshold, all skills in the catalog and both reviewers present on disk, and the new pure-function names plus the two new `_test.go` files match patterns.md conventions and the [009] testable-TUI pattern. The round-1 patterns.md documentation gap is now covered by an explicit Acceptance Criterion. Eight informational findings remain, two of them major: decision rationale still duplicated verbatim in Tasks 2 and 7 (only Task 6 of the three was fixed), and Task 8's new fix-what-you-find mandate combined with `pre-deploy-qa` + `Reviewers: none`, which would let Wave 4 code changes ship unreviewed — the one place where this round's restructure opened something. The six minors are two stale cross-references left by the renumbering (`Decision 8` in Dependencies should be 9; Testing Strategy still calls the stand run a Final Wave task), Task 8's non-concrete file list, three decisions (10, 11, 12) still without Alternatives considered, the unaddressed `because` clause in Task 1, and Task 1's description omitting the 13->12 guard change its own verification row requires.
